1	=========
2	Stability
3	=========
4	
5	Perhaps the trickiest part of finite element modeling is making sure a model is stable. That may
6	sound trivial, but in finite element analysis it is nuanced. If you are getting "singularity"
7	errors in your model, it may not be as stable as you think it is. Remember that just because a
8	model is static does not mean it is stable.
9	
10	Degrees of Freedom
11	==================
12	In 3 dimensions there are 6 "degrees of freedom" for motion to occur in. An object can translate
13	in either the X, Y or Z direction, and it can rotate about the X, Y or Z axis. These 3 translations
14	and 3 rotations together sum to 6 degrees of freedom. For an object to be stable, all 6 degrees
15	of freedom need to be stabilized
16	
17	Instability Type 1: Rigid Body Motion
18	=====================================
19	Rigid body motion occurs when the entire structure can move as a unit in one of the 6 degrees of
20	freedom. This occurs when there is insufficient support for the structure. When rigid body motion
21	occurs, the stiffness matrix is "singular", and unsolvable. Adding supports can eliminate this type
22	of singularity.
